price_issues.message: source_type 'distributor': prefer a manufacturer datasheet, MMPDS/CMH-17 handbook, standard or peer-reviewed source
source_type 'distributor': prefer a manufacturer datasheet, MMPDS/CMH-17 handbook, standard or peer-reviewed source

mass_change.note: mass change of the selected materials (Ashby scaling) is NOT fed back into the sizing loop — use the Pareto sweep / re-size with the chosen material

notes: DAPCA IV database is military/transport aircraft; for light GA prefer Eastlake (Gudmundsson 2014) and treat DAPCA as an upper reference
structure parts: bottom-up process model; final assembly/systems installation NOT included (give final_assembly_hours)
non-recurring engineering/development/flight test taken from Eastlake (no bottom-up model)

calibration.note: Eastlake manufacturing covers the whole airframe (parts, assembly, systems installation) while the bottom-up covers the structural parts — a ratio > 1 is expected; a ratio << 1 means the FOPV parameters (transport-wing parts) overestimate these parts: set labour_calibration from shop data (or 'eastlake')
calibration.labour_calibration_mode: labour_calibration = eastlake: k = 772 h (Eastlake mfg h/unit) / 6348 h (raw bottom-up h/unit) = 0.122 — absolute hours tied to Eastlake (GA CER; extrapolated outside its database, e.g. small UAVs)

L0.method: top-down CERs (modified Eastlake central; DAPCA IV as second CER)
reasons: unmanned (uav_tactical_recce_ucav): both CER databases are crewed aircraft
L0.band_rule: wide end if outside the CER database, narrow end inside; half-way after a cost_L0 calibration

L1.band_rule: wide end with uncalibrated public process parameters or Eastlake anchoring (inherits L0 confidence); middle with a shop labour factor; narrow end after cost_L1 (L2) calibration
L1.note: labour level anchored to Eastlake (L0 → L1, the reverse of the ladder): only the RELATIVE part/process ranking is bottom-up; replace with shop data or L2

fidelity.recommended_why: CERs outside their database: the part/process model is the better basis
fidelity.note: use the recommended level; lower levels are kept for traceability and calibrated by the higher one (cost_calibration)

k_cost_L0_eastlake.what: unit cost L1 bottom-up / eastlake CER (same design, N, USD year)
k_cost_L0_eastlake.note: L1 labour anchored to Eastlake: NOT independent — do not apply

k_cost_L0_dapca4.what: unit cost L1 bottom-up / dapca4 CER (same design, N, USD year)
k_cost_L0_dapca4.note: L1 labour anchored to Eastlake: NOT independent — do not apply

calibration_out.note: ratios higher/lower fidelity of the same design; applied only if the group is listed in manufacturing.cost_calibration.apply (cost_L0, cost_L1)

references.aace_18r97: AACE International (2020). Recommended Practice 18R-97: Cost Estimate Classification System - as applied in engineering, procurement and construction for the process industries, Table 1 (expected accuracy ranges at 80 % confidence: Class 5 L -20..-50 % H +30..+100 %; Class 4 L -15..-30 % H +20..+50 %; Class 3 L -10..-20 % H +10..+30 %; Class 2 L -5..-15 % H +5..+20 %; Class 1 L -3..-10 % H +3..+15 %); generic principles in RP 17R-97. Ranges widen with technological complexity and weak reference data <https://web.aacei.org/docs/default-source/toc/toc_18r-97.pdf> (retrieved 2026-10-28)
references.abbott_mil17: Abbott, R. (2019). Analysis and Design of Composite and Metallic Flight Vehicle Structures, 3rd ed., Sec. 4.1.8 (after MIL-HDBK-17F Vol. 3 Sec. 9.3): ply drop-offs >= 20:1 in the load direction, <= 2 plies per termination; do not buck rivets in composite laminate; fastener edge distance >= 3.0D (2.5D off-axis) in composites <https://www.abbottaerospace.com/aa-sb-001/4-materials/4-1-composite-materials/4-1-8-general-laminate-design-guidelines/> (retrieved 2026-10-28)
references.bao2002: Bao, H.P. (2002). Process Cost Modeling for Multi-Disciplinary Design Optimization. Final report, NASA grant NAG-1-2195 (ODU), Table 4.1 'V0 and tau values for generic wing' (eq. 3.3) <https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20020065232/downloads/20020065232.pdf> (retrieved 2026-10-28)
references.bls_cpi: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, CPI-U, U.S. city average, all items (CUUR0000SA0), annual averages <https://data.bls.gov/timeseries/CUUR0000SA0> (retrieved 2026-10-28)
references.gonzalo2023_b2f: Gonzalo et al. (2023). Automated recycling of unidirectional preimpregnated carbon fibre scraps (Scipedia), citing Blanco et al. (MATCOMP 2018): aeronautical composite parts buy-to-fly 1.1-1.4, scrap up to 30 % <https://www.scipedia.com/public/Gonzalo_et_al_2023a> (retrieved 2026-10-28)
references.gudmundsson2014: Gudmundsson, S. (2014). General Aviation Aircraft Design: Applied Methods and Procedures, Elsevier, Ch. 2 (modified Eastlake model, 2012 USD; labour cost = 2.0969 H R CPI; R_ENG 92, R_TOOL 61, R_MFG 53 USD/h; avionics 15000 USD; piston engine 174 P_BHP; constant-speed propeller 209.66 N D^2 (P/D)^0.12) <https://computationaldesignlab.github.io/aircraft-design/cost/unit_cost.html> (retrieved 2026-10-28)
references.gutowski1994: Gutowski, T.G., Hoult, D., Dillon, G., Neoh, E.T., Muter, S., Kim, E., Tse, M. (1994). Development of a theoretical cost model for advanced composite fabrication. Composites Manufacturing 5(4):231-239 <https://doi.org/10.1016/0956-7143(94)90138-4>
references.nasa_learning: NASA JSC Cost Estimating — Learning Curve Calculator (Wright cumulative-average and Crawford unit theories; aerospace 85 %) <https://web.archive.org/web/20120830021941/http://cost.jsc.nasa.gov/learn.html> (retrieved 2026-10-28)
references.raymer_dapca: Raymer, D.P. (2018). Aircraft Design: A Conceptual Approach, 6th ed., AIAA, Ch. 18 (DAPCA IV, constant 2012 USD): H_E = 4.86 We^0.777 V^0.894 Q^0.163, H_T = 5.99 We^0.777 V^0.696 Q^0.263, H_M = 7.37 We^0.820 V^0.484 Q^0.641, H_Q = 0.076 H_M (cargo) / 0.133 H_M; C_D = 91.3 We^0.630 V^1.3; C_F = 2498 We^0.325 V^0.822 FTA^1.21; C_M = 22.1 We^0.921 V^0.621 Q^0.799; C_eng = 3112 (0.043 T_max + 243.25 M_max + 0.969 T_t4 - 2228); wrap rates R_E 115, R_T 118, R_Q 108, R_M 98 USD/h. Cross-checked against Ozgen (METU AE452 'Cost of an airplane', 2016) and the SI form of the same equations (5.18/7.22/10.5/67.4/1947/31.2 in kg, km/h) <http://ae.metu.edu.tr/~ae452/cost.pdf> (retrieved 2026-10-28)
